critical_code_review_comments: Racking Note flow is well-modeled — DRAFT/RECORDED on RKN side and RACKING_PENDING/RACKED on RN side correctly mirror each other on /record. Both transitions are idempotent (409 on retry).
Defence-in-depth in /record: re-validates location presence + qty>0 even though POST already validates — good (handles the case where a future PUT loosens the check).
Single point of master-data hydration: /record reads from stock_master at record-time and falls back to denormalized RKN item fields (good for robustness if master changes between save and record).
Unique compound index (fy, serial) + DuplicateKeyError retry loop on POST — same pattern as receipt notes — keeps RKN serials race-safe.
Block on RN delete (when any DRAFT or RECORDED RKN references it) is enforced server-side at /api/receipt-notes DELETE, not just UI — good.
Minor: /racking-notes/list does not currently support ?status= filter; not blocking but might be useful for the UI to lazy-load only DRAFT or only RECORDED. (Not in spec, just an enhancement.)

Minor: /api/racking-notes/{id}/record is not idempotent on partial failure — if insert_many succeeds but the racking_notes update_one fails, transactions could exist without RKN being marked RECORDED. Consider wrapping in a Mongo transaction, or at least catching + cleaning up on update failure. Probability is low but worth a note.
